faq.a: Vahid is associated with the Arabic form وَحِيد, whose core sense is vahid; unique, alone.

faq.q: What is the origin of Vahid?
faq.a: Vahid is associated with Arabic. Vahid is Arabic وَحِيد (Waḥīd), meaning 'unique, alone'. It is widely used as a male given name in Iran.
Yes — the underlying form وَحِيد is Arabic.
Vahid can occur in Muslim naming contexts, but it is better described as a Arabic-origin name used within some Muslim naming traditions than as an exclusively Islamic religious term.
Vahid should not be classified as a Quranic personal name without a direct Quranic basis. The root و ح د is Quranic (oneness), but Waḥīd is not itself a Quranic personal name.

faq.q: What does Vahid mean in Urdu?

faq.q: What does Vahid mean in Persian?
faq.a: In Persian, Vahid is rendered وحید and carries the sense وحید، یکتا.
A romanized syllable approximation is va-hid. No IPA transcription is asserted because a verified phonetic transcription was not available.

faq.a: Romanization variants include Vahid, vahid. Script forms are وحيد, وحید, وَحِيد, वहीद.

faq.q: Is Vahid a boy's or girl's name?
faq.a: Documented usage records this form as male. Gender is not inferred from the meaning of the word, and actual use may vary between communities.
